summary: Illinois state forest fire tower near Cypress, Johnson County; announced 1939, described standing on George Bluff in 1957 at 100 ft; now listed as gone; removal date not found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a glass-enclosed observation platform
facts.status_note: Listed as removed; the sources read give no removal date.

visit.trail_note: The tower is gone. The 1957 record places the site on state property; no source describes present-day access.

events.note: Newspaper reports that a 100-foot fire tower will be constructed near Cypress as part of the division of forestry's program
Coast and Geodetic Survey describes the standing state forest fire tower on George Bluff, 100 feet overall

evidence.supports: 1939 report: fire tower to be constructed near Cypress by the division of forestry
evidence.quote: A fire tower will be constructed in connection with the division of forestry's fire protection program near Cypress.

evidence.supports: planned tower 100 feet high, watching private timber in southern Illinois between federal purchase units
evidence.quote: The tower will be 100 feet high and will overlook much of the timber in private ownership between the Shawnee and Illini United States forest service purchase units in southern Illinois.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page heading says Union County, but the survey record on the same page and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list say Johnson County. Johnson is used.

notes_for_editor: Build and removal dates not found; a 1939 newspaper announcement and a 1957 survey bracket the tower. County conflict: the Weebly heading says Union, the survey record and FFLOS say Johnson; Johnson kept, matching the brief. No staffing history found. No new photos found.
